sections.value:
**Security: pass** at `e8bab4e71ad22a2bf4e061a05480dd341ca0e564`.

Accepting port 0 changes port allocation, not exposure or route authority. Default bind remains `127.0.0.1:7461`; client addresses still reject port 0. No C19/C21 disclosure or scoped vulnerability found.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No scoped findings | - |

A non-loopback `:0` request remains subject to the unchanged IP/pairing policy: unpaired remote binds refuse, and paired non-Tailscale/wildcard addresses require explicit `--insecure-bind`. Permitted remote binds remain permitted, not newly trusted (`crates/daemon/src/http/exposure.rs:89-106`). Loopback remains available. Both listeners still share the same router/auth ring and paired-key endpoint scope; selecting an ephemeral port adds no remote API paths.

`boot` obtains the bound address from `TcpListener::local_addr`, substitutes loopback for a permitted wildcard, and creates `bound_config` before building services (`crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:938-954`). BackgroundService receives that actual address and supplies it as `PIJ_RS_ADDR` to jobs (`lib.rs:590-605`; `background.rs:399-408`). It does not trust a caller-reported banner or retain requested `:0`.

Local and GitHub heads agree; worktree clean; PR CLEAN and ready; all five checks succeeded. CI [42471751206](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42471751206) tested a synthetic merge incorporating this head. JUnit artifact [13614275297](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42471751206/artifacts/13614275297) has 2,237 passing cases, no failures, five separately skipped. Confirmed passing: CLI default/ephemeral resolution, actual daemon-log nonzero-port banner, and existing loopback/unpaired/tailnet/insecure exposure cases.

Non-loopback `:0` and background-address flow were source-checked, not independently live-probed. Author mutations were not rerun. No local cargo/builds/tests, daemon/socket/background/pane/process probes, credentials or product edits.
